# Graph-Guided Context Compaction and Dynamic Window Assembly

> Dynamic token budgeting, topological sort serialization, and geodesic path pruning for packing subgraphs into limited LLM context windows.

## Core Findings

- Topological sorting of extracted subgraph contexts produces causal, dependency-ordered prompt serialization that minimizes attention dispersion in autoregressive language models. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172]
- Redundancy-aware graph compaction collapses intermediate bridging nodes while preserving geodesic paths between query entities and factual targets, reducing prompt token consumption by 35%–50%. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04408]
- Dynamic context window budgeting assigns token allocations proportionally to graph community centrality and node degree, preventing peripheral entity noise from displacing core factual evidence. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130]
